bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for in-house upper/sole capacity to enable premiumization and IP protection; Maintaining strong ROCE (16.6%) and ROE (18%); Net debt expected to normalize by FY26 end; No dividend guidance disclosed
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk in Pant Nagar ramp-up; Delay in export market adoption; Oversupply in unorganized segment post-GST; High working capital intensity during peak season; Apparel pilot failure
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; focused on premiumization, capacity control, and long-term brand building; optimistic on GST tailwind and export potential; transparent on phasing and one-offs; no overpromising on margins or export targets
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 8% ASP growth was achieved despite a 12-15% revenue reduction from Flipkart/Myntra business model shift (freight now charged to consumer), indicating true underlying pricing power; Inventory build is seasonal and structural (MSME payment terms tightened to 45 days), not channel stuffing
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Return on Capital Employed of 22.8% is highlighted in the business snapshot; the annual ROCE series reads 18.5%, 30.6%, 23.2%, 19.2%, 22.3%, 22.4%, 22.8% against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, defined as "EBIT divided by Capital Employed".
- Return on Equity series reads 9.0%, 29.3%, 23.9%, 14.9%, 17.2%, 18.1%, 18.0% against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, defined as "TTM PAT by Average Shareholder's Equity".
- Net Debt / EBITDA series reads 1.1, 0.7, 0.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.0 against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, with Net Debt defined as "Borrowings less Cash & Cash equivalent, excludes fixed deposits with banks".
- Reinvestment is framed qualitatively as "Investment in D2C & Tech initiatives" feeding the digitisation flywheel; the deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or a stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Design innovation: in-house design team of 30+ professionals with 1,600+ active styles in circulation and 240+ new designs introduced in FY26
- Vertically integrated supply chain spanning in-house sole and upper manufacturing, enabling a demand-input-to-warehouse lead time of 60-90 days versus an industry average of 90-120 days
- Scaled omnichannel distribution network of 29,000+ retail touchpoints across 800 districts in 28 states, supported by 260+ distributors, 300 EBOs and 2,300+ large-format-store counters
- Culture-led brand building with celebrity-fronted campaigns (Vicky Kaushal, Kriti Sanon) driving rising brand-health metrics (top-of-mind awareness, spontaneous awareness, consideration)
- Approximately 90% domestic raw-material sourcing and 100% in-house final assembly, supporting cost control and supply resilience
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intensified competition — Stiff competition from well-resourced global athletic footwear brands operating in India and emerging domestic D2C players; aggressive pricing, promotional intensity and rapid product iteration by competitors can compress margins and raise customer acquisition costs.
- Raw material and component sourcing — Operational efficiency depends on consistent availability of high-quality inputs (EVA, PU, synthetic uppers, adhesives); disruption or quality deterioration in the supply chain could cause production delays, higher costs and lower consumer satisfaction.
- Commodity price fluctuations — Input costs are sensitive to global commodity movements, particularly petrochemical derivatives underpinning synthetic materials; sharp cost increases may compress margins if not passed through to consumers in a timely manner.
- Fast-changing fashion and trend cycles — Maintaining product relevance in a market shaped by rapidly shifting consumer style preferences requires sustained design innovation and responsive supply chain execution; misreading trend direction could hurt sales velocity and inventory utilisation.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in import duties, BIS compliance standards, GST structures and other regulatory frameworks can alter the Company's cost base and necessitate pricing adjustments; the unresolved inverted-duty structure on certain raw materials remains a cost overhang, against which refund claims have begun to be filed.
- Macroeconomic volatility — Inflation spikes, interest rate increases, currency depreciation or geopolitical disruptions can weaken consumer sentiment and reduce discretionary spending, directly impacting demand for branded and aspirational products.
- Counterfeit goods — Proliferation of counterfeit and imitation products, particularly in mass-market and online channels, poses a risk to brand integrity, consumer trust and revenue.
- Data security — As the Company expands its digital and D2C operations, managing cybersecurity risk and consumer data privacy remains a critical area requiring sustained investment and vigilance.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Double-digit for FY26; Margin: Targeting 16-17% EBITDA margin long-term; Order inflow: Not disclosed; Capex/commissioning: INR 110-115cr in FY26 for Pant Nagar upper plant (3L pairs/month capacity), commissioning by Q4FY26
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Apparel launch (pilot in 60 EBOs in Q3FY26); Export scaling (targeting 5-10% revenue in 2-3 years); Premium sneaker volume growth (100%+ YoY); LFS and defense channel expansion
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- In FY27, scale the new apparel category thoughtfully, deepen the sneaker and women's franchises, extend presence in Western and Southern India, and continue investing in technology, design and talent.
- Deliberate choice of profitability before proliferation in offline retail: held EBO count near 300, corrected store-level unit economics and strengthened franchise partner returns before resuming EBO expansion.
- Completed pivot of the online business from an outright to a marketplace-led model, giving stronger control and better realisations, while remaining the leading footwear brand on major e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms.
- Extension into sports athleisure apparel (launched January 2026 across 60+ EBOs, the brand website, Amazon and Myntra) as a natural extension of design capability, brand equity and distribution network, being scaled with a disciplined, measured approach.
- Continued investment in digital and operational agility (SAP backbone, DMS-led replenishment, field-force applications, daily online replenishment) to move from a made-to-stock toward a made-to-order model.
- The Company has not issued any debt instruments or non-convertible securities; Crisil Ratings revised its outlook on the Company's long-term bank facilities to 'Positive' from 'Stable' during the year, reaffirming 'Crisil A+' (long-term) and 'Crisil A1' (short-term). Employee ownership is maintained through two Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOP 2021 and ESOP 2021 - Vision Pool). BRSR reporting confirms the Company has no subsidiaries or associates.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Commercial production of premium uppers commenced at the Pantnagar facility in January 2026, adding to the Company's integrated premium capacity, while the Paonta Sahib upper facility stabilised fully during FY26. In January 2026 the Company also launched a new athleisure apparel range, initially across 60+ Exclusive Brand Outlets, the brand website and on Amazon/Myntra, as a natural extension of its design capability, brand equity and distribution network. Management states that land and infrastructure are already in place to add manufacturing capacity quickly as demand grows.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's per capita footwear consumption remains well below global averages, with a young, increasingly fitness-conscious consumer base steadily trading up to branded products.
- GST rationalisation during the year was a structural reform for the footwear category; the industry has yet to feel its full demand impact, and management expects it to act as a tailwind as the benefit flows through.
- Sports and Athleisure (S&A) has emerged as the fastest-growing footwear segment in India, now accounting for more than two-thirds of the overall market.
- Branded footwear is expected to achieve parity with the traditionally dominant unbranded segment as organised retail (EBOs, large-format stores, e-commerce) gains traction, supported by 100% FDI and Footwear Park development.
- Premiumisation and a richer product mix (led by the sneaker portfolio) are lifting average selling price and margin, aided by operating leverage and a higher share of premium SKUs.
- Demand across the footwear industry remained softer than anticipated during the year, with discretionary spending yet to recover fully.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's largest and fastest-growing Sports Athleisure (S&A) footwear and apparel companies by both value and volume, built on a design-led, vertically integrated manufacturing and omnichannel distribution platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Campus Activewear designs, manufactures, markets, sells and distributes sports and athleisure footwear, apparel and accessories (socks, backpacks, caps, belts) for men, women and children, sold under the Campus brand and its new sub-brand ELAN by Campus. It serves a broad Indian consumer base across Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities through e-commerce platforms, authorised distributors, exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) and multi-brand outlets (MBOs), with a small export presence.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Premium segment (INR 1,500+): 57.2% of mix (+12pp YoY); Women's: 16.2% of revenue (+2pp YoY); Kids: 4-5%; Accessories: 2-3%; Online: 5.7% growth (impacted by BBD timing shift); Distribution: 20% growth; Export: Nascent, under own brand, pilot in Sri Lanka/Morocco

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Footwear:** Sport shoes (fitness, walking, exercise, light sporting), Sneakers, Casual footwear, Sandals, Slippers, Open footwear
- **Apparel:** Sports athleisure apparel (launched January 2026)
- **Accessories:** Socks, Backpacks, Caps, Belts
- **Sub-brand:** ELAN by Campus (neo-casual footwear collection)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Pan-India, Tier 1/2/3 cities
- International (6 countries, exports ~0.30% of turnover)

capacity.title: Manufacturing capacity (profile)
capacity.body:
| Product / Line | Installed Capacity | Utilised | As of |
|---|---|---|---|
| Footwear (shoe assembly) | 30.7 mn pairs | — mn pairs | FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) |

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: Double-digit for FY26; Margin: Targeting 16-17% EBITDA margin long-term; Order inflow: Not disclosed; Capex/commissioning: INR 110-115cr in FY26 for Pant Nagar upper plant (3L pairs/month capacity), commissioning by Q4FY26

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Apparel launch (pilot in 60 EBOs in Q3FY26); Export scaling (targeting 5-10% revenue in 2-3 years); Premium sneaker volume growth (100%+ YoY); LFS and defense channel expansion

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's per capita footwear consumption remains well below global averages, with a young, increasingly fitness-conscious consumer base steadily trading up to branded products.
- GST rationalisation during the year was a structural reform for the footwear category; the industry has yet to feel its full demand impact, and management expects it to act as a tailwind as the benefit flows through.
- Sports and Athleisure (S&A) has emerged as the fastest-growing footwear segment in India, now accounting for more than two-thirds of the overall market.
- Branded footwear is expected to achieve parity with the traditionally dominant unbranded segment as organised retail (EBOs, large-format stores, e-commerce) gains traction, supported by 100% FDI and Footwear Park development.
- Premiumisation and a richer product mix (led by the sneaker portfolio) are lifting average selling price and margin, aided by operating leverage and a higher share of premium SKUs.
- Demand across the footwear industry remained softer than anticipated during the year, with discretionary spending yet to recover fully.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin improved to 53.9% (up 110bps) due to premium mix and ASP increase; EBITDA margin 14% (rptd), 16% normalized after removing 200bps A&P phasing; Cost of outsourced uppers higher than in-house; Labor cost spike in Haridwar 2 plant (0.4% margin drag) to be neutralized by FY26 end

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for in-house upper/sole capacity to enable premiumization and IP protection; Maintaining strong ROCE (16.6%) and ROE (18%); Net debt expected to normalize by FY26 end; No dividend guidance disclosed

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Commercial production of premium uppers commenced at the Pantnagar facility in January 2026, adding to the Company's integrated premium capacity, while the Paonta Sahib upper facility stabilised fully during FY26. In January 2026 the Company also launched a new athleisure apparel range, initially across 60+ Exclusive Brand Outlets, the brand website and on Amazon/Myntra, as a natural extension of its design capability, brand equity and distribution network. Management states that land and infrastructure are already in place to add manufacturing capacity quickly as demand grows.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; focused on premiumization, capacity control, and long-term brand building; optimistic on GST tailwind and export potential; transparent on phasing and one-offs; no overpromising on margins or export targets

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Design innovation: in-house design team of 30+ professionals with 1,600+ active styles in circulation and 240+ new designs introduced in FY26
- Vertically integrated supply chain spanning in-house sole and upper manufacturing, enabling a demand-input-to-warehouse lead time of 60-90 days versus an industry average of 90-120 days
- Scaled omnichannel distribution network of 29,000+ retail touchpoints across 800 districts in 28 states, supported by 260+ distributors, 300 EBOs and 2,300+ large-format-store counters
- Culture-led brand building with celebrity-fronted campaigns (Vicky Kaushal, Kriti Sanon) driving rising brand-health metrics (top-of-mind awareness, spontaneous awareness, consideration)
- Approximately 90% domestic raw-material sourcing and 100% in-house final assembly, supporting cost control and supply resilience

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk in Pant Nagar ramp-up; Delay in export market adoption; Oversupply in unorganized segment post-GST; High working capital intensity during peak season; Apparel pilot failure

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 8% ASP growth was achieved despite a 12-15% revenue reduction from Flipkart/Myntra business model shift (freight now charged to consumer), indicating true underlying pricing power; Inventory build is seasonal and structural (MSME payment terms tightened to 45 days), not channel stuffing

commitments.body:

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- In FY27, scale the new apparel category thoughtfully, deepen the sneaker and women's franchises, extend presence in Western and Southern India, and continue investing in technology, design and talent.
- Deliberate choice of profitability before proliferation in offline retail: held EBO count near 300, corrected store-level unit economics and strengthened franchise partner returns before resuming EBO expansion.
- Completed pivot of the online business from an outright to a marketplace-led model, giving stronger control and better realisations, while remaining the leading footwear brand on major …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate history] A footnote records that the INR 1,000 mm revenue milestone was "crossed by Nikhil International, whose business was subsequently acquired pursuant to a business succession agreement dated Mar 22, 2017".
- [NCLT merger] Footnote states: "Pursuant to NCLT merger order, EBITDA and PAT for FY'21, FY22, Q1 FY'23 has been revised to give effect to the order."
- [Brand event] "Shoe case 2026" is presented as a brand transformation event unveiling Campus' refreshed brand identity, launching ELAN neo-casual footwear and convening distributor partners nationwide.
- [Elan campaign] The Elan launch is claimed to have drawn "11.7 million+ views: Across Instagram and digital platforms within the first month" and "18 high-quality content pieces driving 127K+ interactions", rolled out across digital, social, retail, Amazon and Myntra with the Amazon Made in India series.
- [Industry source] All market-size and market-share data is attributed to Technopak Advisors' "Report on Footwear Retail in India" dated April 07, 2022, which the deck itself says has not been independently verified.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
